title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review
about: Teacher-verified mastery check. Written separately from the practice generators: different wordings, word problems, and an 'is this right?' item. Each item is worth 1 point. 'math' is the calculation behind the item ('par M' / 'perp M': the slope of a line parallel / perpendicular to a line with slope M; 'par M through X Y' / 'perp M through X Y': that line through (X, Y), as y = mx + b; 'relation M1 M2': whether lines with slopes M1 and M2 are parallel, perpendicular or neither), used only by the test that checks the answer key.
directions: Show your work. Write equations in the form y = mx + b. Write fractions in simplest form.

items.prompt: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to y = (2/3)x − 5?
Are the lines y = 3x + 2 and y = −(1/3)x − 4 parallel, perpendicular, or neither? Explain.
Write the equation of the line through (2, 7) that is parallel to y = 5x − 1.
Write the equation of the line through (4, 1) that is perpendicular to y = 2x + 6.
On a park map, a bike path follows the line y = (1/2)x + 4. A second path will run parallel to it and pass the fountain at (6, 1). Write the equation of the second path.
Lucia says the lines y = 4x + 1 and y = −4x + 3 are perpendicular because their slopes are opposites. Is she right? Explain.
items.answer: Neither (No: perpendicular slopes multiply to −1, and 4 × (−4) = −16; a line perpendicular to slope 4 has slope −1/4)

items.prompt: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to y = −5x + 2?
Are the lines y = 7 − (2/5)x and y = −(2/5)x + 1 parallel, perpendicular, or neither? Explain.
items.answer: Parallel (both slopes are −2/5; the y-intercepts are different)

items.prompt: Write the equation of the line through (−1, 4) that is perpendicular to y = −(1/3)x + 2.
Write the equation of the line through (3, −2) that is parallel to y = −2x + 9.
On a map grid, two railroad tracks run side by side and never meet. One track follows y = 3x − 5. The other passes through the station at (1, 8). Write the equation of the second track.
Kai wants the line through (2, 6) that is perpendicular to y = 2x − 3. He writes y = (1/2)x + 5. Is he right? Explain, and write the correct equation.
items.answer: y = −(1/2)x + 7 (No: he flipped the slope but did not change its sign; the slope is −1/2, and 6 = −1 + b, so b = 7)
